newsitem.title: USA: German climber evacuated from Mount McKinley.
newsitem.headline: German climber evacuated from Mount McKinley.

text.p: Rescuers evacuated a frostbitten German climber by helicopter on Wednesday from the 14,000-foot (4,300-metre) level of Alaska's Mount McKinley, a U.S. National Park Service spokesman said.
Andreas Wendt, 34, of Magdebur, Germany, had been suffering from frostbite for days and had climbed down on his own from 17,000 feet (5,200 metres), Park Service spokesman John Quinley said.
"He had frostbite on all 10 fingers," Quinley said.
Wendt was being taken to an Anchorage hospital, said Daryl Miller, a mountaineering ranger at Denali National Park, site of Mount McKinley, North America's tallest peak at 20,320 feet (6,194 metres).
One climber has died on the peak so far this summer, he said. The body of Mark Trevillyan of Aldershot in Britain was retrieved from the mountain late on Monday, Miller said.
Trevillyan, who fell during a descent from the peak's summit, was killed late on Thursday or early on Friday.
His body was recovered from the mountain's 15,400-foot (4,700-metre) level, at the base of a steep gully, Miller said. Trevillyan's age was not available.
The McKinley climbing season runs from late April to mid-July.
